L377@P3: We take 5 million images sampled from DataComp [18],
L378@P3: processed through a two-step pipeline combining state-ofthe-art MLLM [2] and LLM [1]. First, we employ the
L379@P3: MLLM to generate dense captions, distilling rich visual information into text. Second, we let the LLM synthesize
L380@P3: seven diverse query-target pairs per image using the dense
L381@P3: captions, aligned with MMEB core categories[30]: one for
L382@P3: classification, one for retrieval, and five distinct VQA pairs
L383@P3: composed of two requiring holistic understanding, two focusing on localized details, and one demanding creative reasoning. This process yields 35 million query-target text
L384@P3: pairs and 5 million images. Further details and prompts are
L385@P3: provided in the Sec. D.
L386@P3: 4.2. Single-turn Adaptation of MuCo
L387@P3: Our multi-turn pretraining generalizes to the conventional
L388@P3: multimodal benchmarks [30, 62], having a single querytarget pair per sample. To align with single-query data, we
L389@P3: introduce an adaptive strategy that employs extra contextual dialogue from a given query, allowing MuCo to elicit
L390@P3: its pre-trained multi-turn capability.
L391@P3: We repurpose MuCo to handle single-query pairs. As
L392@P3: shown in Fig. 4, we first establish an initial turn to extract
L393@P3: the initial embedding from the query q or positive target
L394@P3: p. In the following turns, we provide the model with its
L395@P3: masked counterpart (e.g., the masked positive target for a
L396@P3: given query). The model is then explicitly instructed to first
L397@P3: reconstruct the masked parts and generate a subsequent embedding capturing the context of the entire dialogue.
